title: QUEST: A robust attention formulation using query-modulated spherical attention
claim: Under partial input corruption, the baseline's attention collapses onto a few regions and fails, while ours spreads attention across instances and stays correct.
layout: 3x3 grid; columns Image, QUEST, Standard; rows clean, bottom-half noised, top-half noised; green/red prediction labels under each map
description: A 3x3 grid of square images with column headers Image, QUEST and Standard. The left column shows a photo of macaws in foliage. Row 1 is clean, row 2 has the bottom half replaced by colorful random noise, and row 3 has the top half noised. The middle and right columns show jet-colormap class-activation heatmaps over the same inputs. QUEST maps are broad and spread across several birds. Standard maps are sparse and concentrate on a few birds. Under each heatmap is a predicted label. Green 'Pred: Macaw' appears for every QUEST map and for the Standard maps in rows 1 and 2. Red 'Pred: Spoonbil' appears for Standard in row 3. The eye goes first to the red failure label and the contrast between the two heatmap columns.
caption: Class-activation maps for an image from the Macaw class in ImageNet, generated using AG-CAM [ref]. Standard attention concentrates on few bird instances (see first row) and mis-classifies the image if the region containing those instances is noised (see third row). This indicates that the birds in the bottom half of the image do not contribute to the correct prediction in standard attention. Hence, when the top part of the image is noised, the model focuses on the birds in the bottom part of the image since they are the most salient object in the image then, but results in a misclassification. QUEST attention attends evenly to different bird instances and classifies the image correctly even if some of the bird instances are noised. A more diverse attention can make the models more robust to input data variations, which can be observed in the improved model robustness in [ref].
abstract: The Transformer model architecture has become one of the most widely used in deep learning and the attention mechanism is at its core. The standard attention formulation uses a softmax operation applied to a scaled dot product between query and key vectors. We explore the role played by norms of the queries and keys, which can cause training instabilities when they arbitrarily increase. We demonstrate how this can happen even in simple Transformer models, in the presence of easy-to-learn spurious patterns in the data. We propose a new attention formulation, QUEry-modulated Spherical aTtention (QUEST), that constrains the keys to a hyperspherical latent space, while still allowing individual tokens to flexibly control the sharpness of the attention distribution. QUEST can be easily used as a drop-in replacement for standard attention. We focus on vision applications while also exploring other domains to highlight the method's generality. We show that (1) QUEST trains without instabilities and (2) produces models with improved performance (3) that are robust to data corruptions and adversarial attacks.
